## What was tried
IronClaude v5.0.0 is tagged (`d953b983`) and `/sc:post-release v5.0.0` has finished (PR #353, open). What has been checked so far, and what has not:

- **Checked before or at release:** the nine go/no-go checks G1-G9 on the merge commit; a post-merge codegraph check on one real workspace (PASS); a new-user install and a 4.3.5 upgrade in a throwaway HOME (GREEN, all exit codes 0); the full test suite at the tag (14610 passed, 0 failed); the cheap (Tier A) and local-write (Tier B) steps of the 18 hand-test guides, run by the guide writers.
- **Never checked:** every Tier C step (Claude sessions, headless runs, real PRs, proxy, Orca, publishing), any behaviour on the team's other workspaces, macOS or arm64, and any measurement of impact over time (review-loop length, token cost, codegraph use, memory migration, parallel speed-up).

A full breakdown of every new or changed function was written on 2026-11-03: `.dev/releases/current/v5.0.0/impact-breakdown.md` on branch `ironbelly/post-release-v5.0.0`. For each of 18 changes (R1-R18, covering all 45 capabilities of the release inventory) it states the **desired** impact (author's intent), the **predicted** impact (from code and recorded runs) and what is still **unvalidated**, each with file:line evidence. Summary, highest risk first:

| Rank | Change | Desired | Predicted (evidence) | Still unvalidated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Review severity rule: minor findings never fail; every review loop stops after 2 fix cycles (3 reviews), then escalates | End review loops of 4-8 rounds spent on wording and citation nits | Rule text in `src/superclaude/output-styles/pragmatic.md:225-229`; old "any severity" wording gone; `/sc:implement` one A2 repair (`refs/retry.md:142`); CI guard `tests/skills/test_review_severity_rule.py` | Loop length after release; real defects passed as "minor"; escalation rate; reviewer template still has no codegraph guidance |
| R2 | `/sc:pr-submit` defaults to `--monitor 3` (pushes fixes without asking), Codex support, origin-first target, PR-head check | Fewer manual fix rounds; never a PR on the upstream parent; never push unreviewed commits | `DEFAULT_MONITOR = 3`, guards `pr_head_ok`, `push_parent_ok` in `src/superclaude/pr_submit/fsm.py` | No controlled run of levels 1-3, `pr_head_mismatch`, or Codex re-review; quality of auto-pushed fixes |
| R3 | codegraph installed by default (required install phase) and Serena / codebase-memory registrations retired | One code-intelligence server on every machine, old registrations cleaned without deleting user data | Pin 1.6.2 with SHA-256 check; 10 s / 15 s retire bounds; `serena-local` kept; e2e GREEN | Success across team workspaces; macOS/arm64; Coder images that re-add Serena |
| R4 | Upgrade is `install --force`; `superclaude update` and plain `doctor` are not enough | One command to a complete 5.0.0 | Plain `doctor` passes with no codegraph (`src/superclaude/cli/doctor.py:164`); `--force` overwrites edited `~/.claude` files | How many installs are half-upgraded today; lost local edits |
| R5 | codegraph used by commands, skills and agents; new `/sc:graph`, `/sc:impact` | codegraph answers symbol, caller and impact questions as leads that are Read before citing; Grep/Read fallback stays; never blocks; narrow tool list to limit tokens (no source claims "faster or more accurate than Grep") | Kill switch and fallback in `src/superclaude/core/CODEGRAPH.md`; one real troubleshoot run used codegraph tools; about 12% estimated risk of a long `/sc:implement` loop via an empty graph answer (estimate, zero observed sample) | Answer quality, real token cost, call rate, false-absence events |
| R6 | Session memory moves from Serena to `<project>/.superclaude/memory/`; `.serena/memories/` read-only for one release | Memory without an MCP server | Paths in `commands/save.md:42`, `load.md:42-43` | Real save/load across sessions; projects still holding only `.serena/memories/` |
| R7 | Sprint: auto-resume by default, per-task handoff, `--resume`, `--task-parallelism` | Resume without redoing work; faster parallel runs | `CI=0` counts as yes (`sprint/commands.py:325-326`); `--resume` skips nothing with shipped defaults (gate mode `off`, outcome `pending`) | Speed-up of parallelism; CI scripts without `--yes`; tmux flag dropping |
| R8 | codegraph SessionStart auto-index hook | Every checkout indexed on first session | About 70 KB per file, up to about 1 GB memory on first init (changelog) | Real time, memory and disk on team repos |
| R9 | ccsession: per-worktree list (#347), shim survives its terminal (#341), one session name, names per repo, `ccsession-orca` | No wrong-worktree resumes; no cut replies when a terminal closes | Shim calls `os.setsid()`; rename hook registered; guide Tier B passed with a stand-in | Real Orca/Coder use; old shims still running |
| R10 | `reflect run`: bounded `--fix` loop, promote by default | Self-fixing audit gate | Defaults confirmed in code; no 5.0.0 run can return `halted`, so `--fix` never applies a fix (N5) | Any useful auto-fix; live proxy reviewers |
| R11-R12 | Remediation routing to `/sc:workflow` then `/sc:implement`; `/sc:reflect` flags removed, contract 1.8.0 | Lighter default fix path | `troubleshoot.md:54` documents the plan route; post-release used it on 66 tasks | Real sessions offer it and never auto-execute |
| R13 | Routing guide `HOW-WE-WORK.md`, shorter `CLAUDE.md`, six core files retired | One routing source, less context | Files shipped / removed as stated | `/sc:recommend` and `/sc:help` route sample goals correctly |
| R14 | ccsession tier rules by role, letter tiers, published model data | Central per-role model access | Schema 2, 256 KiB cap, env overrides in `skills/ccsession-tag/models.py` | Live shim and publish to master (E01 Step 10, E02 Steps 11 and 13) |
| R15-R18 | Pipelines (swarm, eval, prd, cli-portify), freshness hooks, issue templates, LiteLLM opt-in, unchanged commands | Varied | 35 known defects: O1-O23 from code reading, the e2e run and the test suite; N1-N12 from the guide runs; only O1 (#352) and N7 (#29) have open issues | Defects reproduce; follow-up issues filed |

## Done when
1. Clay has reviewed the runbook below and posted on this issue either "approved as is" or the changed version (rows added, removed, thresholds or owners changed).
2. Clay has delegated each runbook row to William or Leandro and said so on this issue.
3. Every approved row has been run, and its result is posted on this issue as one comment per row: row id, date, who ran it, the measured value, the baseline, PASS or FAIL against the threshold, and the evidence (command output or the guide step's Pass/Fail box).
4. Every FAIL, and every known defect (O1-O23, N1-N12) a row confirms, has its own follow-up issue on `IronbellyOrg/IronClaude`, filed from a filled copy of `~/.claude/ISSUE-BACKLOG.md` with `gh issue create --repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude --body-file <copy>`, and linked here.
5. Clay has posted a short closing summary: which desired impacts were confirmed, which were not, and what to change.

## Who it is for
**Clay** (assigned). Please:

1. **Review** the runbook below against the breakdown file. Check the metrics, baselines, thresholds and owners.
2. **Approve it or change it.** Post "approved as is", or post the changed rows. Three thresholds are proposals that need your call: the 2,000-token codegraph budget (RB5), the 2% ceiling on `/sc:implement` tasks reaching a 4th attempt (RB1), and the 140 KB-per-file index-size flag (RB8). Also rule on one open point: `docs/testing/v5.0.0/user/D07-pr-submit.md:115` runs `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` with no `--repo`. It is the pre-PR check the repository `CLAUDE.md` requires, but it breaks the post-release plan rule that every `gh` command in a doc names `--repo`, and it keeps the post-release plan package from archiving.
3. **Delegate** each approved row to William or Leandro and say who has which row on this issue. The "Who" line of each row is a proposed split by track (William: install, codegraph, memory, ccsession, routing; Leandro: review loops, PRs, sprint, reflect, pipelines, hooks); change it as you see fit.

### Runbook (highest risk first)

**Before you start (every tester):**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude.git ~/v5-impact/IronClaude
cd ~/v5-impact/IronClaude && git remote -v   # must show only origin = IronbellyOrg/IronClaude (no upstream remote)
gh pr checkout 353 --repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude
superclaude --version   # must print 5.0.0
```

- Follow "Safety rule: throwaway HOME" in `docs/testing/v5.0.0/README.md`. Steps tagged `[LOCAL-WRITE]` use a throwaway `HOME` or `/tmp`. Steps tagged `[CLAUDE-SESSION]` or `[API-LONG]` run in your real install and the installed hooks write `~/.claude/state/` and `~/.claude/logs/`; D08 shows how to move a session into a throwaway HOME.
- `[EXTERNAL]` steps only on a sandbox branch or a throwaway repo. Every `gh` command names `--repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude` or the throwaway repo.
- Cost tags (lowest to highest): `[FREE]` read-only, seconds; `[LOCAL-WRITE]` writes in a throwaway HOME or `/tmp`; `[CLAUDE-SESSION]` interactive Claude session, uses tokens; `[API-LONG]` headless `claude` runs, uses tokens; `[PROXY]` needs `T2ProxyUrl`, `T2ProxyKey`, `T2Model0N`; `[EXTERNAL]` creates a PR, issue, push or uses an operator service.
- **Two checkpoints:** run every guide step and survey now (T0). Re-run the window scans (RB1, RB2, RB5b, RB16) and the RB3/RB4 workspace survey 14 days and 42 days after the team upgrades.
- Post each row's result as a comment here (row id, date, who, measured value, baseline, PASS or FAIL, evidence).

---

#### RB1. Review severity rule and 2-fix-cycle cap (R1, High)

- **Metric:** (a) QA gates outside `/sc:implement` that reached a 4th review; (b) `/sc:implement` tasks that reached attempt 4 or more, and what blocked them; (c) the static guard; (d) real defects passed as "minor"; (e) escalation at the cap.
- **How:** in each project repo where reviews ran after the upgrade:

  ```bash
  # (a) numbered QA reports created after the tag date
  find .dev -name 'qa-*report-[0-9]*.md' -newermt 2026-11-02 -printf '%h %f\n' \
    | sed -E 's/-report-([0-9]+)\.md$/ \1/' \
    | awk '{k=$1" "$2; if($3>m[k]) m[k]=$3} END{for(k in m){t++; if(m[k]>=4){h++; print "4+ reviews:", k}} print "qa_gates="t+0, "gates_with_4plus_reviews="h+0}'
  # (b) /sc:implement ledgers: highest attempt per task, and halts
  #     (plan packages under .dev/tasks/, and runs on a file or prompt under .dev/implement/)
  for f in .dev/tasks/to-do/*/progress.md .dev/tasks/done/*/progress.md .dev/implement/*/progress.md; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    awk -v f="$f" '/^T[0-9A-Za-z.-]+: retry n=/{t=$1; sub(":","",t); match($0,/n=[0-9]+/); n=substr($0,RSTART+2,RLENGTH-2)+0; if(n>m[t]) m[t]=n}
      /^T[0-9A-Za-z.-]+: (complete|blocked)/{t=$1; sub(":","",t); c[t]=1}
      END{for(t in c){tot++; if(m[t]>=4) hi++} printf "%s tasks=%d attempt4plus=%d\n", f, tot, hi+0}' "$f"
  done
  grep -H 'halt review=' .dev/tasks/*/*/progress.md .dev/implement/*/progress.md 2>/dev/null
  # (c) static guard, from the IronClaude clone
  uv run pytest tests/skills/test_review_severity_rule.py -q
  ```

  (d) Take 10 findings graded minor after 2026-11-02 (from `artifacts/retries/T*/notes.md` in plan packages, or PASS-with-notes QA reports). A second person re-grades each against the definition in `src/superclaude/output-styles/pragmatic.md:225`. (e) D06 Steps 1-2 `[FREE]`; optionally D06 Step 9, a seeded defect that cannot be fixed (`/sc:implement` keeps its own ladder, so its Expected result is a last ledger line `T1: halt review=<2-5>` with no `complete` line).
- **Baseline:** measured in the IronClaude repo on 2026-11-03 with the commands above but without `-newermt`: 2 of 14 numbered QA gates had 4+ reviews; `/sc:implement` ledgers: 3 of 8 tasks reached attempt 4+ in `TASK-WF-implementTheAppr-20261024-060449` (old rule; two of them ended `halt review=5 reason=ladder-end`), 0 of 175 tasks in the other 14 ledgers (8 plan packages, 6 under `.dev/implement/`). From `.dev/releases/current/v5.0.0/QA-LOOP-FINDINGS.md`: 4 of 60 tasks had 4+ rounds under the old #277 rule, 0 of 45 under #297; two ad hoc loops ran 7 and 8 rounds.
- **Pass threshold:** (a) 0 gates with a 4th review; (b) at most 2% of tasks reach attempt 4+ (proposed; Clay to confirm), and each has a blocking finding, never a minor one, as its cause; (c) all tests pass; (d) 0 of 10 re-graded minors are real defects; (e) D06 Step 9 matches its Expected result.
- **Who:** Leandro (proposed). **Cost:** `[FREE]` for (a)-(d); `[API-LONG]` for D06 Step 9.

#### RB2. `/sc:pr-submit` level 3 by default (R2, High)

- **Metric:** PR target owner; PR-head and push guards; level 0-3 behaviour; auto-pushed fixes later reverted or redone.
- **How:** D07 Steps 1-4 `[FREE]`, Step 5 `[LOCAL-WRITE]`, Steps 6-13 `[EXTERNAL]` on a sandbox branch of `IronbellyOrg/IronClaude` (close the sandbox PR afterwards). In the window:

  ```bash
  gh pr list --repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude --state all --limit 500 --search "created:>=2026-11-02" --json number,url --jq '.[].url'
  gh pr view <N> --repo IronbellyOrg/IronClaude --json commits --jq '.commits[].messageHeadline'   # each PR where /sc:pr-submit pushed
  ```

  Each tester also checks the URL printed by every `/sc:pr-submit` they run.
- **Baseline:** the guides said `--monitor 1` (propose only) before 5.0.0 (`CHANGELOG.md:224`); a PR landed on the upstream parent on 2026-05-25 (repository `CLAUDE.md`).
- **Pass threshold:** every D07 step matches its Expected result; 100% of PR URLs start with `https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/`; Step 8 halts with `pr_head_mismatch`; no push adds more than one commit on top of the PR head; 0 auto-pushed fix commits reverted in the window (each one that is gets an issue).
- **Who:** Leandro (proposed). **Cost:** `[EXTERNAL]`.

#### RB3. codegraph install phase and retire step (R3, High)

- **Metric:** install exit codes; codegraph registration on every workspace; retired registrations; nothing removed that should be kept.
- **How:** D01 Steps 1-22 (`[FREE]` then `[LOCAL-WRITE]` in a throwaway HOME), or re-run the recorded e2e from a plain terminal with no Claude session open on that machine (this also settles finding O22):

  ```bash
  bash docs/testing/v5.0.0/c-e2e-run.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/c-e2e-rerun.txt; grep '^SUMMARY' /tmp/c-e2e-rerun.txt
  ```

  The script hardcodes Coder-image paths (`/home/coder`, `/usr/local/bin/claude`, `uv`, `node`), so it runs only on a Coder workspace as user `coder`; elsewhere use D01 Steps 6-22.

  Read-only survey on each team workspace (also used by RB4):

  ```bash
  superclaude --version
  superclaude install --list | grep -iE 'codegraph|User registration|Ready for Serena|serena|codebase-memory'
  superclaude doctor --verbose | grep -iE 'codegraph|legacy|retired'
  ```

  If anyone has a Mac or an arm64 machine, run D01 Steps 6-13 there.
- **Baseline:** `SUMMARY s1_install=0 s1_doctor=0 s1_second=0 s2_install=0 s2_doctor=0` (`docs/testing/v5.0.0/c-e2e-transcript.txt:799`); A3 check PASS on one workspace.
- **Pass threshold:** SUMMARY all 0 and no `REAL_HOME_CHANGED`; every workspace shows 5.0.0, a `User registration:` that is not `absent`, `Ready for Serena retirement: yes`, and no `no codegraph registration` line; 0 `serena-local` or user-changed registrations removed; macOS/arm64 recorded as tested or "not tested".
- **Who:** William (proposed). **Cost:** `[FREE]` survey; `[LOCAL-WRITE]` D01 and e2e (network: GitHub and the codegraph download).

#### RB4. Upgrade completeness across the team (R4, High)

- **Metric:** number of workspaces that are half-upgraded (5.0.0 files without codegraph, or retired registrations left), old core files left, edited files overwritten.
- **How:** the RB3 survey, plus on each workspace:

  ```bash
  ls ~/.claude/ORCHESTRATOR.md ~/.claude/COMMANDS.md ~/.claude/PERSONAS.md ~/.claude/MODES.md ~/.claude/FLAGS.md ~/.claude/MCP.md 2>/dev/null
  ls -d ~/.claude/skills/codebase-memory 2>/dev/null
  cmp ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/v5-impact/IronClaude/src/superclaude/core/CLAUDE.md && echo "CLAUDE.md is the 5.0.0 copy"
  ```

  D01 Steps 17-18 (`update` is not enough; `install --force` completes it) and Step 21 (`./update.sh`).
- **Baseline:** none exists; the T0 survey is the baseline.
- **Pass threshold:** every half-upgraded workspace is listed here and its owner told to run `superclaude install --force`; at the 14-day checkpoint 0 remain. Leftover retired core files and the `codebase-memory` skill are listed (harmless; owner decides).
- **Who:** William (proposed). **Cost:** `[FREE]`.

#### RB5. codegraph in commands, skills and agents; `/sc:graph`; `/sc:impact` (R5, High)

- **Metric:** (a) tokens per session added by the codegraph registration; (b) how often sessions call codegraph tools vs Grep/Read; (c) `/sc:impact` completeness; (d) blocking review findings caused by an empty or unread graph answer.
- **How:**

  ```bash
  # (a) six short headless calls in a scratch repo; compare the medians
  mkdir -p /tmp/cg-tok && cd /tmp/cg-tok && git init -q
  jq '{mcpServers:{codegraph:.mcpServers.codegraph}}' ~/.claude.json > /tmp/cg-tok/cg.json
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0 claude -p "Reply with the word ok." --output-format json --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' \
      | jq '.usage | .input_tokens + .cache_creation_input_tokens + .cache_read_input_tokens'
    SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_AUTOINIT=0 claude -p "Reply with the word ok." --output-format json --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config /tmp/cg-tok/cg.json \
      | jq '.usage | .input_tokens + .cache_creation_input_tokens + .cache_read_input_tokens'
  done
  # if jq prints null, read the field names from the `usage` object and sum the input-token fields it shows
  # (b) tool calls in session transcripts since the upgrade
  find ~/.claude/projects -name '*.jsonl' -newermt 2026-11-02 -print0 \
    | xargs -0 grep -ho '"type":"tool_use","id":"[^"]*","name":"[^"]*"' \
    | sed 's/.*"name":"//; s/"$//' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -30
  ```

  (c) D03 Steps 13-16 `[CLAUDE-SESSION]`; in the D03 fixture, compare every caller `/sc:impact` lists with `grep -rnw <symbol> .` on the indexed source files. (d) In plan packages created after 2026-11-02, `grep -ril codegraph .dev/tasks/*/*/artifacts/` and read each blocking finding that mentions it. Also D03 Steps 1-12 and 17-18 (`SUPERCLAUDE_CODEGRAPH_PRIMITIVES=off` degrades but never stops).
- **Baseline:** (a) hiding `codegraph_explore` saved about 1,861 tokens per session in four headless runs (`CHANGELOG.md:92`); no figure exists for the seven registered tools. (b) none; one recorded troubleshoot run used codegraph tools (`A3-RESULT.md:12`). (d) the QA-loop investigation estimated about 12% risk over 3 months, observed sample zero.
- **Pass threshold:** (a) median difference ≤ 2,000 tokens (the changelog's proposed limit; Clay to confirm); (b) recorded, no threshold until Clay sets one after T0; (c) 0 call sites missed in indexed source; (d) 0 blocking findings caused by an empty or unread graph answer; D03 all PASS.
- **Who:** William (proposed). **Cost:** `[API-LONG]` (a, six short calls); `[FREE]` (b, d); `[CLAUDE-SESSION]` (c, D03).

#### RB6. Session memory migration (R6, Medium-High)

- **Metric:** projects that still hold only `.serena/memories/`; save/load correctness.
- **How:** survey (set the root to where your projects live):

  ```bash
  find ~/workspaces -maxdepth 6 -type d -path '*/.serena/memories' 2>/dev/null | while read -r d; do
    p=${d%/.serena/memories}
    if [ -d "$p/.superclaude/memory" ]; then s=migrated; else s=NOT-migrated; fi
    echo "$s $p $(ls "$d" | wc -l) files"
  done
  ```

  D04 Steps 1-9 (Step 6: `.serena/` must stay unchanged).
- **Baseline:** none; the T0 survey is the baseline. `/sc:load` reads `.serena/memories/` for this release only (`docs/releases/v5.0.0.md:173`).
- **Pass threshold:** D04 all PASS; every `NOT-migrated` project with files has an owner decision posted here before the next release.
- **Who:** William (proposed). **Cost:** `[FREE]` survey; `[CLAUDE-SESSION]` D04.

#### RB7. Sprint auto-resume, handoff, `--resume`, `--task-parallelism` (R7, Medium-High)

- **Metric:** guide behaviour; wall-clock gain of `--task-parallelism 2`; CI scripts that now stop.
- **How:** D10 Steps 1-13 (`[FREE]`, `[LOCAL-WRITE]`), Steps 14-17 `[API-LONG]`; put `time` in front of the `superclaude sprint run` command in Step 14 (Run 1) and Step 16 (Run 3). CI survey (set the root to your projects):

  ```bash
  grep -rnE 'superclaude sprint (run|rerun-tasks)' --include='*.sh' --include='*.yml' --include='*.yaml' --include='Makefile' ~/workspaces 2>/dev/null | grep -v -e '--yes' -e ' -y'
  ```

- **Baseline:** before 5.0.0 a bare `sprint run` started at phase 1; `--start 1` keeps that behaviour (`docs/releases/v5.0.0.md:156`). Known as coded: `--resume` skips nothing with shipped defaults (N2) and `CI=0` counts as yes (O7).
- **Pass threshold:** every D10 step matches its Expected result (N2 and O7 recorded and filed, not counted as a failure of this row); Run 3 real time is lower than Run 1 (record the ratio); every CI script found without `--yes` or `CI=1` is listed and its owner told.
- **Who:** Leandro (proposed). **Cost:** `[API-LONG]`.

#### RB8. codegraph auto-index hook cost (R8, Medium)

- **Metric:** first-index time, peak memory and index size per file on 2-3 real team repositories.
- **How:** on a fresh clone in `/tmp` (never in a working repo):

  ```bash
  git clone --depth 1 <repo URL> /tmp/cg-cost/repo
  time uv run --no-project python -c 'import resource,subprocess,sys; subprocess.run(["codegraph","init","--yes",sys.argv[1]],check=True); print("peak_rss_kb", resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss)' /tmp/cg-cost/repo
  du -sk /tmp/cg-cost/repo/.codegraph
  codegraph status /tmp/cg-cost/repo   # only after init has exited; gives the indexed file count
  ```

  D03 Steps 5-8.
- **Baseline:** about 70 KB per indexed file and up to about 1 GB of memory during the first init (`CHANGELOG.md:93`).
- **Pass threshold:** peak RSS ≤ 1,048,576 KB; `.codegraph` size ÷ indexed files ≤ 140 KB (twice the stated figure; proposed, Clay to confirm); time recorded per repo; D03 Steps 5-8 PASS.
- **Who:** William (proposed). **Cost:** `[LOCAL-WRITE]`.

#### RB9. ccsession: per-worktree list, shim, names, Orca (R9, Medium)

- **Metric:** guide behaviour; wrong-worktree resumes; shims still running pre-fix code.
- **How:** D08 Steps 1-13 (`[FREE]`, `[LOCAL-WRITE]`), Steps 14-17 `[CLAUDE-SESSION]`. Shim age on each workspace:

  ```bash
  for p in $(pgrep -f local-gateway-alias-proxy.py); do ps -o pid=,lstart=,user= -p "$p"; done
  stat -c '%y' ~/.claude/skills/ccsession-tag/local-gateway-alias-proxy.py
  ```
